rules.reason: Importing UI components into services couples server-side logic to browser rendering. This breaks SSR, testability, and separation of concerns.
rules.whatBreaks: Server-side services gain browser-only dependencies. Unit tests for services fail. SSR breaks.

rules.description: Controllers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Direct DB access in controllers bypasses the service layer. This breaks the layered architecture and makes logic untestable.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic leaks into controllers. Database coupling makes refactoring expensive.

rules.description: Route handlers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Routes should delegate to services/controllers, not query the database themselves.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic scattered across route files. Impossible to test in isolation.

rules.description: UI components cannot import server-only modules.
rules.reason: Server-only modules may contain secrets or Node.js-only APIs that crash in the browser.
rules.whatBreaks: Build errors in browser environments. Potential secret exposure.

rules.description: High-impact clusters (Config) must not gain new circular dependencies.
rules.reason: High-impact clusters already coordinate many modules. Adding circular imports makes builds fragile.
rules.whatBreaks: Module resolution fails. Build tools (webpack, esbuild) may hang or produce incorrect output.
examples: Use dependency injection or an event bus to break cycles.

rules.reason: Changing the encryption algorithm or key derivation method makes all existing encrypted data unreadable.
rules.whatBreaks: Encrypted data (tokens, at-rest fields, backups) cannot be decrypted.

rules.description: Payment processing (PCI-DSS) — all Stripe/payment code requires compliance review.
rules.reason: PCI-DSS requires that all payment card data handling meets security standards. Any change to payment flows must be reviewed.
rules.whatBreaks: PCI compliance violation. Payment processor account suspension. Legal liability.
examples: Always review PCI-related code before merging.
